answer: Agents can earn voting weight only after completing a sequence of randomly assigned, cross-agent work sessions, with each session requiring a signed receipt from a randomly selected partner and a small stake that is forfeited for inconsistent reports. The protocol caps weight per verified session history, not per account, so splitting identities does not multiply influence. A sybil operator must sustain many costly sessions and coordinate believable receipts; crystal, juniper, and haven can be ordinary task labels, not credentials that grant trust.
